intro: Ojalá with three tenses: a hope, a wish against reality and a regret.
p.ojalá.consejo: It always asks for the subjunctive. Its tense changes the meaning: hope, unreal wish or regret.
p.ojalá hubiera.consejo: With a participle it expresses a regret: what did not happen and you wish had. It equals «I wish I had».
p.debería haber.consejo: It is a reproach or regret: «debería haber llamado» says you did not call. It goes with a participle.
p.tendría que haber.consejo: It means almost the same as «debería haber»: something necessary that was not done.
p.me arrepiento de.consejo: «Arrepentirse» goes with «de»: «me arrepiento de no haber ido». It is a pronominal verb.
p.de joven.consejo: It means «when I was young». It does not change by gender: a man or a woman says it the same.
p.idioma.consejo: It is masculine although it ends in -a: «el idioma». The stress falls on «dio».
p.piano.consejo: The «ia» sounds like one beat: PYA-no. It is masculine: «el piano».
p.nunca es tarde.consejo: It is a saying: it is never too late to start something. «Nunca» before the verb already negates.
p.empezar.consejo: It changes e to ie: «empiezo». The z becomes c before e: «empecé».
p.antes.consejo: It never changes: «antes», «mucho antes», «un poco antes».
b1.texto:
**Ojalá** changes meaning according to the tense that follows:

- **Ojalá venga** mañana. → a possible hope (present subjunctive).
- **Ojalá estuviera** aquí. → something that is not so now (imperfect subjunctive).
- **Ojalá hubiera estudiado** más. → a regret about the past (pluperfect subjunctive).

The last two equal «I wish…» in English.
b2.f0.texto: I wish I had more free time.
b2.f1.texto: I wish I could travel all year.
b2.f2.texto: When I was young I gave up piano lessons.
b2.f4.texto: I wish I had not given them up.
b2.f5.texto: I should have learnt another language.
b2.f7.texto: I regret not having started earlier.
b4.texto:
The three uses of **ojalá**:

- Hope: **ojalá** + present subjunctive. Ojalá **llueva**.
- Wish against reality: **ojalá** + imperfect subjunctive. Ojalá **tuviera** más tiempo.
- Regret: **ojalá** + **hubiera** + participle. Ojalá **hubiera ido**.

A softer wish: **me gustaría que** + imperfect subjunctive. Me gustaría que vinieras.

For a reproach or regret about the past: **debería haber** or **tendría que haber** + participle. Debería haber llamado. Also: **Deberías habérmelo dicho**.

After **arrepentirse de** comes an infinitive: me arrepiento de **no haber ido**.
b4.e2.texto: I wish I had studied more.
b5.f0.texto: In the living room of the old house, a black piano sleeps under a white sheet.
b5.f1.texto: Lucía lifts the cloth and discovers some yellowed keys.
b5.f2.texto: A deep note comes out of the wood and trembles in the still air.
b5.f3.texto: The memories arrive slowly, with a smell of wax.
b5.f4.texto: On the wall, an old photograph shows the girl she once was.
b5.f5.texto: She should have practised every afternoon, as her aunt asked her to.
b5.f6.texto: She sits on the stool and rests her hands fearfully on the keys.
b5.f7.texto: Her fingers find on their own the beginning of a simple melody.
b5.f8.texto: A pale sun comes in through the window and draws a square on the floor.
b5.f9.texto: The music sounds clumsy, but it fills the house with an old joy.
b6.o0.refuerzo: «Venga» is a possible hope about the future.
b6.o1.refuerzo: «Estuviera» speaks of now, not of a past.
b6.o2.refuerzo: Yes! «Hubiera estudiado» regrets something that was not done.
b6.pregunta: Which sentence expresses regret about the past?
b7.o0.refuerzo: Correct: a wish against reality takes the imperfect subjunctive.
b7.o1.refuerzo: «Tengo» is indicative and «ojalá» does not accept it.
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Tendría» is conditional and does not follow «ojalá».
b7.pregunta: You want something you do not have now.
b8.traduccion: I wish I had not given them up
b9.o0.refuerzo: «Llueva» leaves the possibility open: it may happen.
b9.o1.refuerzo: That's it: «estuviera» says that he is not here.
b9.o2.refuerzo: «Esté» is a hope: you do not know whether he is.
b9.pregunta: Which sentence says it is NOT so now?
b10.frase: Me arrepiento de no ____ empezado antes.
b10.o0.refuerzo: Exactly: «no haber empezado» is the compound infinitive.
b10.o1.refuerzo: «He» does not go after «de»: an infinitive is needed.
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «I wish I could travel.»
b12.o0.refuerzo: It is advice for now or for tomorrow.
b12.o1.refuerzo: Well done! «Haber» plus participle looks at the past: you did not call.
b12.o2.refuerzo: It is a present obligation, not a reproach.
b12.pregunta: Which sentence reproaches something that already happened?
p.dejé.consejo: Past tense of «dejar», first person. The accent marks «yo».
p.arrepientes.consejo: With «tú», the verb takes the -es ending: «te arrepientes».
p.empezado.consejo: The participle of «empezar». After «haber» it describes something that already began.
p.sábana.consejo: Do not confuse it with «sabana», a grassland, which has no accent.
p.teclas.consejo: Plural of «tecla». The c before a sounds like k.
p.amarillentas.consejo: Made from «amarillo» with «-entas», a little of that colour, in feminine plural.
p.quieto.consejo: The «qu» sounds like k, and «ie» is one sound: KIE-to.
p.cera.consejo: In Spain the c before e sounds like th; the r is a soft single tap.
p.fotografía.consejo: The accent on the i splits the vowels: fo-to-gra-FI-a.
p.practicado.consejo: The participle of «practicar», used after «haber»: «debería haber practicado».
p.tía.consejo: The accent on the í splits the vowels into two syllables: TI-a.
p.taburete.consejo: A seat with no back. The r between vowels is a single soft tap.
p.apoya.consejo: From «apoyar». The final y sounds like «ya».
p.solos.consejo: Plural of «solo»; it agrees with the subject, so it ends in -s.
p.sencilla.consejo: Feminine form of «sencillo»; the ll sounds like y.
p.pálido.consejo: The accent makes the first syllable the stressed one: PA-li-do.
p.torpe.consejo: It refers to hands or body, not to the mind.
p.haberme.consejo: Infinitive of «haber» with «me»: «Deberías haberme llamado» means you should have called me.
